title: Use cases
blurb: Real experiments, virtual experiments and the hybrid training case.
text: Use cases TMS NeuroPilot is one controller with four run modes. The GUI, relay protocol and analysis are the same in all of them; only the hardware behind the roles changes. This page maps the modes to the ways teams use the suite. Use case Coil Neuronavigation Stimulator MEP Command Real experiment, robot robot InVesalius real real EMG neuropilot robo Real experiment, manual operator InVesalius real real EMG neuropilot manual Virtual experiment virtual robot sim nav virtual virtual EMG neuropilot sim Operator training operator InVesalius real virtual EMG neuropilot training Real experiment The production path. The subject is prepared as described in Subject data; InVesalius tracks the coil and the head, the robot driver moves the coil, the stimulator fires, and the EMG computer records the response. TMS NeuroPilot runs the mapping loop and analyses each pulse. Use the robot when the coil must be held precisely for many placements: Use manual mode when the operator holds the coil, when the robot is unavailable, or when you want to isolate a robot problem from the rest of the pipeline: The operational checklist is in Real session checklist; the manual workflow is in Manual mode. Virtual experiment No hardware and no subject. The simulated stack starts the relay, the virtual neuronavigation, the virtual robot and the controller in one terminal: The controller runs the same state machine and the same analysis as a real session. The E field comes from the project library (or the online solver), and the virtual EMG turns that field into a synthetic MEP at the configured channel sources. Use it to: learn the GUI and the mapping loop without a subject; develop and debug the controller, relay, robot or analysis; reproduce a real session problem with the same code paths; demonstrate the system and train new operators. Start with Quick start, then follow A simulated session for the wire level walkthrough. Operator training The in between case: a real stimulator and coil on a printable phantom, real InVesalius tracking, the operator holding the coil, and no real EMG. The MEP trace is synthesized from the E field, so the trainee sees and hears real pulses and works through the real positioning, navigation and safety loop while the response and the R² map are simulated. Start the production relay and InVesalius, then the controller: No robot driver and no EMG PC are needed. launch relay starts the production relay from TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH as in robo mode. E field and sources The channel sources are project data, exactly as in the virtual twin: the project defines which cortical element drives which channel. The Config › Simulation page shows the configured channels and the sources file; edit the mapping in the Project tab. Precomputed mode uses the library row for the target, like a simulated session. Online mode uses the field computed from the realised coil pose, like a real experiment. The stimulator amplitude is the real amplitude set in the session, so the synthetic MEP scales with it. The installation is one command; the manual recipe, the Windows notes and the optional components are one link away. The simulated stack running in one terminal (relay, virtual neuronavigation, virtual robot and the controller) and one mapping session in which the controller has driven the robot, fired the stimulator, analysed the EMG and rendered an R² map on a cortical surface mesh. A real session uses InVesalius for the neuronavigation and tms robot control for the robot; this page stays with their virtual twins. 1. Get the code The example subject lives in its own repository ( tms neuropilot data ): 2. Install with one command The only prerequisite is conda (miniforge or miniconda) on the PATH. title: Units and frames
blurb: Millimetres, degrees, head space, robot base and the coil-handle convention.
text: Units and frames Most "the robot went to the wrong place" reports are a units or frame mistake, not a robot fault. This page states the conventions once, so the rest of the site can refer to them. The two unit systems Context Length Rotation Where Relay messages millimetres degrees, intrinsic XYZ Euler ( sxyz ) every position / orientation field MuJoCo scene metres radians sim robot internals, MJCF assets SimNIBS files millimetres degrees (matrix) m2m , ROI HDF5, placements, E field library URDF metres (file may differ; ikpy converts) radians sim robot/assets/urdf/ Coil model .ccd millimetres its own frame SimNIBS coil library The conversion points are few and deliberate: controller/pipeline controller.py converts a matsimnibs 4×4 matrix to (position mm, euler deg) with transformations.euler from matrix(m, "sxyz") before anything is sent. sim robot converts mm/degrees at its relay boundary and works in SI inside. The 3 D viewer converts nothing: it reads the same SimNIBS space mesh the analysis uses, so mesh, placements and E field columns share one frame. The frames Frame Origin and axes Used by SimNIBS head space the subject's T1, NIfTI convention (x right, y posterior, z superior), mm mesh, ROI, placements, E field, exported coordinates Neuronavigation space InVesalius' patient space after registration markers, tracked coil, "coil at target" Robot base frame the robot's own base, metres motion planning in tms robot control Coil local frame origin at the stimulation point, handle along −y coil model, tool chain, IK target The robot's tool centre point (its end effector site — coil tcp site in the shipped model) is the coil's stimulation point, not the flange and not the handle. If you change the coil mount, re measure the tool point before the next real session. A tool point error moves the focus by exactly that error. The coil handle convention The coil's local −y axis points along the handle, away from the head. The robot's IK orients the coil with that convention; the 3 D viewer draws the handle segment using the same axis. A coil whose handle is drawn in the wrong direction is usually a transpose in an orientation matrix, not a modelling error. Reading a target A target is a 4×4 matsimnibs matrix: The position is t . The orientation is R . When a file stores many targets the layout is (4, 4, n) — one matrix per placement, index aligned with the rows of the E field library . This is why sorting the placements reorders the E field rows and the target order file together (see Coil placements). Checklist before trusting a target [ ] The mesh, the placements and the E field library come from the same SimNIBS run of the same subject. [ ] The number of placements equals the first dimension of E mag . [ ] The number of E field columns equals the number of ROI triangles. [ ] The target order file only contains indices in 0 … n placements 1 . [ ] In simulation, the coil visibly touches the head at the target. [ ] In a real session, the neuronavigation's registration was accepted and the coil is inside the tracking volume at the first target. Next Coil placements and target order — the files these conventions apply to. Add a robot — where the base pose and tool site are declared.

title: Prerequisites
blurb: Python, Qt, SimNIBS, a display and the hardware a real session needs.
text: Prerequisites What kind of machine Requirement Details Operating system Linux. The suite is developed and used on Debian/Ubuntu; macOS and Windows are not tested. Display A graphical session (X11, or Wayland with XWayland). The controller is a PyQt5 application and needs a display; headless runs only make sense for the test suite. Python 3.11, in a conda environment named neuropilot throughout this documentation. Disk 6 GB for the environment and SimNIBS; subject meshes and E field libraries add several GB per subject. RAM 8 GB is enough for the simulator and the GUI; a full SimNIBS head mesh and the online solver are happier with 16 GB. GPU None required. The 3 D view uses OpenGL; Mesa's software renderer is fine for everything except smooth interaction with a million triangle mesh. Software Piece Needed for Comes from Python 3.11 + pip everything conda / miniforge PyQt5, qasync the controller GUI and its event loop conda forge pyvista , vtk the 3 D cortical view conda forge / pip pynibs MEP extraction and the fit functions pip (GitLab) h5py , numpy , scipy every data file conda forge python socketio , aiohttp the relay client pip python dotenv , pyyaml configuration pip mujoco , pybullet , ikpy the virtual robot pip SimNIBS 4.5 the online E field solver and .msh meshes SimNIBS wheel + MKL/MUMPS magicpy driving the stimulator (MagVenture) pip (vendor package) smbprotocol reading the EMG files from the acquisition PC pip InVesalius real mode and training neuronavigation separate conda env tms robot control real mode robot driver + production relay separate checkout (from the authors) pynibs and magicpy are lab packages; if pip install pynibs cannot find them on PyPI, install them from a local wheel or ask the authors for a checkout. The suite imports them lazily, so the simulator runs without magicpy . Knowledge You should be comfortable with: a terminal and a conda environment (activate, install, run); editing a YAML file without breaking indentation; the TMS basics: coil orientation, motor threshold, MEP, resting motor territory, why the coil needs to stay on target. You do not need to know SimNIBS, FEM, Qt or robot kinematics to run the simulator; the site explains what each file is for. For a real session only The full hardware list is on Hardware setup. In short: the TMS robot, the neuronavigation camera and PCs, the stimulator, the EMG amplifier and a network that connects them. None of it is needed to install or explore the software. TMS NeuroPilot has no medical approval. Real stimulation requires ethics approval, a trained operator, the stimulator's own safety limits and the subject's written consent. Do not use it to make clinical decisions. Next Install the suite Hardware setup

InVesalius, the neuronavigation application for real sessions, has its own environment; its installation is at the end of this page. Quick install The repository ships a one file environment spec and an installer that does everything below (optionally including InVesalius): or by hand: That is it — neuropilot starts the suite and opens the mode selector; neuropilot sim starts the simulated stack directly. The numbered sections after this one walk the same steps in detail and explain what each package is for; they remain the reference when something in the quick path fails on your machine. Manual installation 1. Get the code The repository is self contained: src/ holds the four packages, scripts/ the data preparation tools, docs/ the documentation sources. The example subject lives in its own repository — clone it into place only if you want to run the example pipeline: 2. Create the environment That is the minimum for the simulator and the GUI. The exact package set of an existing lab machine is a superset; if you are migrating, conda list on the old machine is the reference. Install the lab packages If the package index does not have them, install the wheels the group provides or take them from the lab share. Check what is missing with: 4. One known good recipe, all inside neuropilot : 5. text: Subject data A session needs five artefacts for one subject. This page says what each one is, which script produces it, and what TMS NeuroPilot checks when it loads it.

title: E-field library
blurb: Build the precomputed E-field HDF5 and understand what the solver stores.
text: E field library The E field library is the precomputed half of the mapping: for every coil placement, the electric field it produces at every triangle of the ROI. The controller reads one row per pulse, so a pulse is always associated with the field of the pose that delivered it. The same file is the training data for the surrogate E field estimator — the interpolation method of Grosshagauer et al., 2025 — and the source for the ParaView field comparisons. What the file contains e.hdf5 from scripts/02 create roi efield library.py : Dataset Shape Meaning E mag (n placements, n elements) float field magnitude per placement and ROI triangle, V/m at 100 % stimulator output E (n placements, n elements, 3) float field vector, optionally E norm (n placements, n elements) float normal component, optionally E tan (n placements, n elements) float tangential component, optionally target (3,) float the target position the search was centred on, mm The controller requires E mag with shape (placements, elements) . Extra datasets are ignored by the regression but useful for inspection. A 500 placement library with all four datasets is roughly 350 MB as float64; a dense surrogate library (some thousands of placements) is several GB. Keep one library per subject and ROI. The bundled example subject is stored through Git LFS; generated libraries for study subjects should not be committed. Building it The script centres the search automatically: without target it uses the ROI centroid, and without search radius it derives the radius from the ROI extent (the largest distance from the target to an ROI triangle centre) plus a 10 mm motion margin. Both can be set explicitly when a session needs something else. Flag Default Meaning mesh msh required SimNIBS FEM mesh roi hdf5 , roi idx required, midlayer m1s1pmd pynibs mesh HDF5 with roi surface/<idx coil required coil model .ccd target ROI centroid search centre, mm, SimNIBS space search radius ROI extent + margin mm around the target margin 10.0 extra radius for the automatic search radius, mm n placements 500 placements to keep; 0 keeps the full grid search angle 180.0 handle rotation range, degrees angle resolution 7.5 step of the rotation search, degrees spatial resolution 3.0 step of the position search, mm distance 1.0 coil to scalp distance, mm target radius 1.0 target tolerance, mm anisotropy scalar scalar or vn (needs a DTI tensor) solver pardiso FEM solver dadt at nodes nodes (fast) or elements (reference) didt 1e6 dI/dt used to scale the field, A/s out e.hdf5 output path The script runs one FEM solve per placement. With the default node based dA/dt a solve takes 2–3 s on the ernie mesh (the elements reference path 4× longer). Expect minutes for a 500 placement library and hours for a dense surrogate grid. Progress is printed per placement and flushed on purpose; run with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 when redirecting the output. The output records how it was produced: target source , roi radius mm , search radius mm , margin mm , the grid resolutions, plus the mesh, ROI, coil and solver settings. A library can always be traced back to the run that produced it. Recipes Precomputed library (the default): a 3 mm / 7.5° grid subsampled to 500 placements. This is the file the Precomputed E field mode loads. Surrogate library (dense grid): no subsampling, 4 mm spacing and 15° rotations, covering the ROI plus the motion margin. This is the training data for the E field surrogate — the interpolation method of Grosshagauer et al., 2025 (EfieldInterpolation) — and for the ParaView comparison; several GB and a few hours are normal. The original a priori step uses APSim (the auxiliary dipole method) and stores the field at the target; this library is computed with the OnlineFEM solver and keeps every ROI triangle, which is what the per element interpolation and the R² map need. title: Coil placements and target order
blurb: The placement library, the target-order file and how the loop consumes them.
text: Coil placements and target order The placements file says where the coil can go . The target order file says where it goes next . Both are index aligned with the E field library, which is what keeps the regression consistent. The placements file search positions.hdf5 from SimNIBS TMSoptimize (or the group's wrapper): Dataset Shape Meaning matsimnibs (4, 4, n) float one coil matrix per placement, mm, SimNIBS space centers (n, 3) float, optional coil centre per placement m0 , m1 , m2 (n, 3) float, optional coil axes, for inspection The controller reads only matsimnibs . Each matrix follows the convention in Units and frames: translation is the stimulation point, rotation columns are the coil axes. Row i of matsimnibs is column i of E mag . If you sort, subsample or filter the placements, you must apply the same reordering to the E field library. sort coil placements.py exists for exactly this reason — see below. The target order file A plain text file with one integer per line: Rules: indices into the placements file, 0 based (the first placement is 0 ); one target per line; whitespace and blank lines are fine; values must be integers and 0 <= index < n placements ; the file is validated when you load it, not when you press Start. An invalid file is rejected with a message naming the offending index: If you do not load an order file, the controller stimulates all placements in file order — useful for a first test, slow for a real session. The order file may repeat an index. A protocol that alternates between two hot spots, or returns to the best target at the end, is just a longer list. Choosing an order scripts/03 create optimized sequences.py selects a subset of placements that constrains the regression well and writes an order file: Flag Default Meaning e hdf5 required the E field library to select from n stim 500 number of pulses to plan out dir next to the library where the order files are written seed 42 RNG seed for the random baseline dataset E mag which field dataset to use normalize none feature normalisation before selection rbf tau , rbf ridge auto , 0.0 RBF kernel width / ridge for D optimal w pos , w ang 2.0, 1.0 travel cost weights (position mm, angle deg) no auto sort off keep the selection order instead of travel sorting It writes one file per strategy ( RANDOM , FPS , D Optimal , …) plus a travel sorted.txt variant. Use the travel sorted file : the robot spends most of its time moving between targets, and a spatially coherent order roughly halves the session duration. Sorting placements for travel If you already have a placement file and an order, reorder both together: The script writes a new matsimnibs file, the matching order file and an XDMF for visual inspection. Use the outputs as the project's targets file and target order fn ; do not mix the sorted order with the unsorted library. Common mistakes Symptom Cause references target N, but only M placements exist order file is 1 based or from another subject contains non integer entries a header line, a comma separated list or a float every pulse uses the same field order file lists one index repeatedly map looks spatially scrambled sorted placements paired with an unsorted library robot takes a long path between targets raw algorithm order instead of travel sorted.txt Coil at target never arrives placement is outside the robot's reach or collides Next EMG channels and MEP windows The project file

title: EMG channels and MEP windows
blurb: Channel names, cortical sources, sampling rate and the extraction window.
text: EMG channels and MEP windows The controller does not record EMG itself in a real session; it reads what the EMG acquisition wrote and extracts the MEP (CED/Signal in the reference setup). Two things must therefore agree: the names and count of the channels , and the window in which the response is searched. Channel names and count EMG CHANNELS in .env : The list drives: the labels on the MEP plots, the columns of the results CSV ( mep FDI mV , …), the number of channels the cortical map offers, the number of entries the channel source YAML must have. The channel list is read at import time. Changing it in Config › Study shows the new value, but the running controller keeps the old list until it is restarted. The status line says needs restart for this reason. The channel source file A small YAML referenced by the project's emg config fn , one entry per channel, assigned positionally to EMG CHANNELS : Field Meaning element id 0 based index into the ROI triangles, also the E field column index xyz position in mm in SimNIBS space; the nearest ROI triangle centre is used The number of entries must equal the number of channels. A mismatch is rejected and the previous channel assignment stays in use. Both cases are reported in the log. The source ties a muscle to a cortical site, which is what makes the map per channel rather than a single global fit. It does not change where the coil goes; that is the placements file. The MEP window All values live in .env and are read at import time: Key Default Unit Meaning SAMPLING RATE 4000 Hz acquisition sampling rate CUTOFF FREQ 500 Hz low pass filter before extraction TMS PULSE TIME 5 tenths of a second time of the pulse in the recording (5 → 0.5 s) START MEP 10 samples window start, relative to the pulse END MEP 100 samples window end, relative to the pulse MEASUREMENT START TIME 0 samples first sample kept from the file With the defaults the MEP window is (100 − 10) / 4000 = 22.5 ms long. A cortical MEP typically starts 20–30 ms after the pulse; make sure the window covers the response for the muscle and the latency you expect, not just the default. What pynibs computes The windowed signal is filtered at CUTOFF FREQ , the peak to peak amplitude is taken over the window, and the result is reported in mV. A window that contains no response yields a small amplitude, not an error — that is a real result and appears in the table like any other. The pre activation period (before the pulse) is displayed on the MEP page but is not used by the regression. The virtual EMG (simulation and training) In simulation and training the "EMG" is generated from the E field and the channel sources: the virtual amplifier adds noise and a recruitment curve on top of the field at the channel's source element. The source element is read for every pulse, from the precomputed row or from the online per pulse field. Two response models are available: DVS (the default): a sigmoid in the E field itself. x0 and the slope are in V/m, and the input side noise is also in V/m. TVS : the nine coefficient population model. Its input is E / upper limit (a fraction of maximum stimulator output); p3 – p7 are the linear coefficients from the original model. The settings are .env keys, read when the controller starts: Key Default Effect VIRTUAL MEP MODEL dvs dvs or tvs VIRTUAL MEP NOISE MV 0.001 white noise sigma added to the trace, mV VIRTUAL MEP TRIAL VARIABILITY true trial to trial variability of the MEP model VIRTUAL MEP MT 60 field at or below which no MEP is produced, V/m VIRTUAL MEP UPPER LIMIT 100 TVS normalisation field, V/m VIRTUAL MEP EFIELD SCALE 1.4 scale applied to the precomputed E field row DVS keys: VIRTUAL MEP DVS X0 (V/m), VIRTUAL MEP DVS R (per V/m), VIRTUAL MEP DVS SIGMA X (V/m), VIRTUAL MEP DVS AMP (mV), VIRTUAL MEP DVS Y0 (mV), and VIRTUAL MEP DVS SIGMA Y (log10 units). TVS keys: VIRTUAL MEP TVS P1 … P9 . p1 / p2 are log10 terms; p3 – p7 are linear values, p8 is V, and p9 is dimensionless. VIRTUAL MEP MT rem

headings: The file is the session record
text: The project file A project is one YAML file per subject and session. It points at the subject's files and carries the stimulation and mapping defaults. Load and Save on the Project page read and write it; everything in it can also be edited by hand. An annotated project Every key Key Type Default Meaning project name string file name label shown in the title bar and used as the default save name mesh head path path none SimNIBS .msh or HDF5 head mesh mesh RIO path path none ROI surface HDF5 ( geo.hdf5 ) coil path path none SimNIBS .ccd coil model targets file path none placements HDF5 with matsimnibs target order fn path none target order text file; all placements when absent e field path path none precomputed E field library ( E mag ); unused online surrogate library path path none dense library for the Interpolated mode ( E mag + roi hash ); needs mesh RIO path emg config fn path none channel source YAML results fn path none CSV written when the session finishes overwrite results bool true replace an existing results fn ; when false, an existing file is kept and the final table is written to <name <stamp .csv fit fun string Linear one of the nine fit shapes; see Analysis and fits map elms int 1 analyse every n th ROI element (subsampling) stimulator amplitude int 20 % MSO stimulator waveform string Biphasic Biphasic or Monophasic n repetitions int 1 pulses per target minium isi int 4 minimum inter stimulus interval, seconds default speed int 40 robot speed while travelling, % tuning speed int 10 robot speed near the head, % efield mode string absent Precomputed , Online or Interpolated ; carried with the subject collision test mapping or null null accepted cell layout: head position m , head orientation deg , robot base position m , robot base orientation deg , start joints rad , branch (shoulder, arm, wrist), safe height mm , translation threshold mm , rotation threshold deg ; null means no setup was saved mesh RIO path (capital RIO) and minium isi (missing "m") are the keys the code has used since the first version. They are what existing project files contain, so they are what the GUI reads and writes. Renaming them would invalidate every saved project; treat them as the format, not as typos to fix. Loading Project › Load accepts .yaml and .yml . A file that is not a mapping (empty, a list, a binary file, a corrupt YAML) is refused with a message; the current project stays loaded and usable. Keys that cannot be coerced to the widget type are skipped with a warning; the rest of the file still applies. Loading is refused while a mapping is running — swapping the library or the subsampling under a live analysis would change what the map means. After a successful load the path is remembered and restored on the next start ( /.neuropilot/last session.yaml , or the path in NEUROPILOT SESSION FILE ). Saving Project › Save writes plain YAML, in the order shown above. An empty project name adopts the file name. .yaml is appended when the dialog returns a name without an extension. A failed write (folder deleted, permission denied) leaves the project marked as unsaved; pick another location. Paths Use paths relative to the project file for files inside the subject folder, and absolute paths for files outside it. The loader expands and resolves a relative path against the directory of the project YAML. When the GUI saves a project, it stores a path relative if the asset is below the project file and absolute otherwise. This keeps a copied subject folder portable without hiding where external dependencies live. For a project generated by a script, write the paths in the YAML relative to the YAML itself. The project loader does not depend on the controller's working directory. The file is the session record The project file plus the results CSV are the record of a session. The CSV holds what happened (poses, amplitudes, MEPs, E field mode per pulse); the YAML holds what was planned. Keep both, and keep the E field library they refer to

title: Study profiles
blurb: One protocol file for mapping, stimulation and analysis defaults.
text: Study profiles A study profile is the protocol layer: the values that stay the same for every subject of a study, as opposed to the project file, which is per subject. It is a small YAML edited on Config › Study . What it holds Key Default Meaning fit fun Linear regression shape used for the R² map map elms 1 subsampling: analyse every n th ROI element efield mode Precomputed default E field mode for the session: Precomputed , Online or Interpolated pulse shape Biphasic stimulator waveform n repetitions 1 pulses per target min isi 4 minimum inter stimulus interval, seconds amplitude 20 stimulator output, % MSO sampling rate 4000 EMG sampling rate, Hz cutoff freq 500 EMG low pass, Hz tms pulse time 5 pulse position in the recording, tenths of a second start mep 10 MEP window start, samples after the pulse end mep 100 MEP window end, samples after the pulse emg channels FDI,APB,ADM channel names, comma separated An example: Save, load, apply The three buttons on Config › Study are deliberately separate: Button What it does Save study… writes the current values to a YAML (default <data folder /study.yaml ) Load study… reads a YAML into the widgets — nothing changes in the session yet Apply to session pushes the widget values into the live controls This two step flow lets you inspect a profile before it changes a running session. The status line reports exactly what happened: What applies immediately fit function and subsampling, pulse shape, repetitions, minimum interval, amplitude, the E field mode (if that mode is available). What needs a restart MEP windows ( sampling rate , cutoff freq , tms pulse time , start mep , end mep , measurement start time ), EMG channel names . The controller parses these at import time, so the running process keeps the old values. The status line always lists them under needs restart . Check that line rather than the widgets. What is refused Apply to session does nothing while a mapping is running: Changing the fit function or subsampling mid run would change the meaning of the map that is being built; the controller refuses instead of producing a mixed result. Where to keep it Default location: <ROOT FOLDER /study.yaml , which makes it available to everyone using that data folder. A study with several protocols can keep one file per protocol ( study rest.yaml , study online.yaml ) and load the right one per session. The study profile is not copied into the project file. Save both: the project says which subject, the study says which protocol. Relationship to .env Some study values also exist as environment keys ( EMG CHANNELS , SAMPLING RATE , …). The precedence is: Applying a profile writes into the live controls; it does not edit .env . If a value in .env pins the same key, the next restart returns to the .env value. That is intentional: a lab that pins a key in .env should not be overridden by a colleague's study file. Next Settings model — the full precedence picture. Config page — the four scopes in the GUI.

title: Run modes
blurb: Simulation, real hardware and manual mode: what differs and when to use which.
text: Run modes TMS NeuroPilot has four run modes. They share the controller, the state machine, the relay protocol and the analysis; they differ only in who provides the robot, the neuronavigation, the stimulator and the EMG. Run neuropilot with no arguments to choose a mode in the selector, or start a mode directly with neuropilot sim , neuropilot robo , neuropilot manual or neuropilot training .

title: A simulated session
blurb: Follow one mapping from Connect to Complete in the virtual twin.
text: A simulated session This is the full walkthrough of one mapping session in the simulator: what you click, what appears in the log, and what the controller is doing on the wire. It assumes the stack is running (Quick start) and a project is loaded. Before Start 1. Connections : all four cards green. In simulation they turn green a second after the controller connects; if one stays grey, press Reconnect . 2. Control — choose Precomputed E Field . The hint under the radios says "Precomputed library — ready immediately." and Start becomes enabled. 3. Set Amplitude and Repetitions . For a first session the defaults are fine; n repetitions: 1 keeps it short. 4. Cortical results — the ROI mesh is displayed. No map is shown yet. Start is enabled only when the robot (or manual mode), the stimulator, the EMG and the E field mode are all ready. A grey Start is a status, not a bug: the hint under the E field radios says which condition is missing. Press Start The first target appears in the status line: and the log shows: The controller now runs the seven steps for this target: Step What happens What you see SEND MARKER sends the coil pose to the neuronavigation as a marker Sending target to InVesalius! START TRACKING waits 3 s for the nav to be ready, then asks the robot to press — WAIT FOR TARGET REACHED waits for Coil at target the robot arm moves in the MuJoCo view FIRE STIM fires the stimulator a pulse marker on the EMG trace COLLECT DATA records the EMG, extracts the MEP, stores the field row a new row on the MEP results page ANALYSE appends the pulse to the regression R² appears after three pulses COMPLETE next repetition or next target a new === BEGIN TARGET === block While it runs The Control page shows the current target, the pulse count and the log. The MEP results page draws the live trace and the peak to peak trend. The Cortical results page redraws the map after each analysis task. You can: Action Effect Pause holds before the next pulse; the coil stays on target Start resumes from where it stopped Next skips the current target and moves to the next order entry Back repeats the previous target (ignored while a pulse is in flight) Move Coil Up stops, pauses and retracts the robot Finish ends the session after the current step, writes the results Pause is checked before the pulse, not only between targets. The robot keeps the coil on the head while paused, so a subject can relax without losing the target. When something is unhealthy If a system drops out mid run, the loop holds instead of aborting: The operator can fix the system (press Reconnect ) and the loop continues: Finish is always available during a run, even when a system is dead — a session must always be stoppable. Finishing Press Finish . The controller stops after the current step, retracts the robot, waits for the final analysis and writes the results CSV to the project's results fn : The controller does not print a "written" line; check the file's modification time or open it. In simulation, finish with a handful of pulses and open the CSV — one row per pulse with the realised pose, the amplitude, the MEP per channel and the E field mode. See Export and data formats. What the log tells you A healthy target looks like this (abridged): With fewer than three pulses the analysis step says so instead of fitting: A pulse whose realised pose never arrives from the neuronavigation is dropped rather than recorded with the wrong geometry: The timeout is COLLECT TIMEOUT S (default 20 s). While the controller is waiting for the robot, there is no timeout: use Next to skip the target or Finish to end the session. Next The mapping loop — the same loop, in detail. E field modes — switch to online mid session.

title: Real session checklist
blurb: The ordered checklist for a session with a participant.
text: Real session checklist This is the operational page. It assumes the installation, the subject data and the lab wiring are done; the goal is that nothing about the software is decided for the first time while a subject is in the chair. TMS NeuroPilot has no medical approval. Real stimulation requires ethics approval, a trained operator, the stimulator's own safety limits and written consent. This checklist covers the software, not the medical procedure. The day before [ ] Ethics approval and consent form are on file for this protocol. [ ] T1 and T2 MRI scans acquired for the subject. [ ] SimNIBS head mesh ( m2m <subj ) and ROI surface ( geo.hdf5 ) created. [ ] Candidate coil placements ( search positions.hdf5 ) and the E field library ( e.hdf5 ) created. [ ] Coil placement optimization chosen and run; the target order file is generated. [ ] The prepared files pass the sanity checks. [ ] A study profile is saved with the intended fit function, ISI, amplitude and MEP windows. [ ] The E field mode is decided: precomputed (library ready) or online (solver loads in about a minute). One hour before [ ] Production relay available. neuropilot robo starts it automatically when TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH is configured and no relay is running; otherwise it asks for the checkout. [ ] InVesalius available. It starts automatically by default; press Is started if it runs on another machine, or use no invesalius . [ ] Robot driver running: python main loop.py . [ ] Controller running: neuropilot robo (or neuropilot robo launch relay , kept for compatibility). [ ] Connections page: relay, stimulator, EMG and robot all green. [ ] Project page: the project loads without an error dialog. [ ] Cortical results : the mesh is displayed and the coil model is loaded. [ ] Stimulator armed and the amplitude shows the value you expect. [ ] The robot's force sensor shows a reading (touch it once if the robot side says Awaiting valid pressure data ). neuropilot sim starts all four simulated peers. In robo mode TMS NeuroPilot starts the controller, the production relay when it is configured, and a local InVesalius. The Relay card can also start or restart a relay that TMS NeuroPilot owns. main loop.py remains a separate application and must be started as above. Five minutes before [ ] Subject seated, head supported, coil cable routed with slack. [ ] Neuronavigation registration accepted; the coil is tracked. [ ] Emergency stop within reach of the operator. [ ] Control page: E field mode selected, Start enabled. [ ] Amplitude, repetitions, minimum interval and pulse shape match the protocol. [ ] Stop criteria are written down and visible (see below). During the session Watch the Control log, not only the 3 D view. A pulse is only fired when the coil is at target, the force is above the threshold and the minimum interval has elapsed. If a system drops out, the loop holds: Held at <step : <system not ready. Finish ends the session. Fix it, press Reconnect , and the loop continues. Pause holds before the next pulse; the coil stays on the head. Next skips a target, Back repeats the previous one. A pulse in flight cannot be taken back ( Previous ignored: a pulse is in flight. ). Stop the session with Move Coil Up and then Finish if the subject reports discomfort, the coil overheats, the robot faults, the subject moves out of tracking, or the MEPs disappear without an explanation. The software cannot decide this for you. Ending 1. Press Finish . The controller finishes the current step, retracts the robot and waits for the last analysis. 2. Wait for We are done. in the log. 3. Confirm the results CSV exists and is not empty (path shown on the Project page under Results file ). 4. Export the R² table and the placement log from Cortical results if the analysis needs them: Export CSV… . 5. Stop the controller, then main loop.py , then InVesalius, then the relay. After the session [ ] Results CSV copied to the study folder and backed up. [ ] R² export and placement log copi

title: Collision test
blurb: Find a subject position, robot base and start pose that survive every placement before a real run.
text: Collision test Long coil handles and a subject who can only sit a few ways make robot cell layout a real constraint. The Collision test page lets you find a subject position, robot base and start configuration before a real experiment, using the selected robot model in a local MuJoCo scene. It does not stimulate, record EMG, fit a map or talk to the real robot. The page is available in every mode that has a robot. It is disabled in manual and training modes, where there is no arm to test. What it checks the robot and coil holder against the subject head phantom; robot self collision; every placement in the project's placement file, in file order; the direct joint space path from the start pose and then from one placement to the next. It pauses at the first collision and leaves the arm at that pose, so you can see what hit. The head and robot base can then be moved, the coil raised with Move coil up , or another branch selected, and the same scan resumed. An IK failure still stops the scan because there is no colliding pose to inspect. Placements are converted with the same pipeline to robot axis convention as the simulated robot and then into the robot base frame, so the planned world pose and an executed target agree even after the base is moved. Method The scene is compiled from the selected robot's MJCF model and the subject skin surface. MuJoCo evaluates contacts and nearest distances; ikpy solves the same URDF chain that the simulated robot uses. The scan follows the production direct or upward rule. It compares the largest per axis translation with TRANSLATION THRESHOLD (millimetres) and the largest per axis rotation with ROTATION THRESHOLD (degrees). If either limit is exceeded, the arm climbs to SAFE HEIGHT (millimetres), traverses above the head and descends. Otherwise it uses a direct joint space line. There is no separate 20 mm retract waypoint. Each segment is sampled at 30 waypoints and every waypoint is checked. The same three values are also used by the manual move away and emergency paths, where the arm always climbs to SAFE HEIGHT . A head penetration of 4 mm or more and a self penetration of 2 mm or more count as collisions. The 4 mm head allowance matches the production simulation, where the coil is pressed into the scalp. Head clearance of 10 mm or less is not reported as a near miss, because the coil is often close to the scalp; the always on contact colour overlay shows that clearance on the links. Self collision ignores overlaps shallower than 2 mm. The robot's collision meshes overlap by about 1 mm at some wrist configurations even though the rendered links look clear, so these shallow self contacts are treated as mesh overlap. A self penetration of 2 mm or more still pauses the scan. This tolerance is a modelling limit, not a hardware safety margin. MuJoCo is described in Todorov, Erez and Tassa (2012), MuJoCo: A physics engine for model based control , IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems. ikpy is a pure Python inverse kinematics library built on the URDF joint chain. The scene contains the head phantom only. It does not model the subject's shoulders, torso, chair or the room. The path is a joint space interpolation, not the production controller's exact trajectory. The real robot controller and its force/safety limits remain the final authority. Enable it Press Enable collision test . The first enable builds the local world and IK chain; later scans reuse it. The page also loads the project head mesh and converts its skin surface to an STL, so the phantom matches the subject. The 3D view uses the same embedded renderer as the simulated robot view. Drag to orbit, right drag to pan, wheel to zoom, double click to reset. Its top right overlay mirrors the Control page: Total targets and Current show the same pulse 0 · 1/1 · target 44 counters. The path waypoint is in the status line below the scan controls. The collision test checks the target geometry; it does not fire sti

title: Manual mode
blurb: Hardware without the robot: the experimenter positions the coil.
text: Manual mode Manual mode runs the real pipeline without the robot: a person holds the coil, the neuronavigation tracks it, and the controller waits for Coil at target exactly as it does with the robot. or neuropilot controller manual when the relay, InVesalius and the stimulator are already running. What changes Real mode Manual mode Robot process required not started Robot card on Connections present absent Start gate waits for the robot ignores the robot Coil positioning robot the operator Pressure signal force sensor not used Coil pose robot forward kinematics tracked coil from the neuronavigation Everything else identical identical The controller sets manual = True , which: skips Press robot button messages, skips the force threshold check in WAIT FOR TARGET REACHED , keeps the minimum interval and coil at target gates, takes the realised pose and the aim error from the tracked coil instead of the robot's forward kinematics; the pose columns are filled as usual, the pressure column is not. The workflow 1. Make the relay and InVesalius available as in robo mode; neuropilot manual starts them automatically when configured. 2. Start the controller: neuropilot manual . 3. Load the project. 4. On Control , choose an E field mode. Both work; precomputed still needs the library and the placements. 5. Press Start . The controller creates the first marker. 6. Move the coil until the neuronavigation reports Coil at target . 7. The controller fires when the interval has elapsed. The sequence then repeats for the next target. With a precomputed library the coil must be at the planned pose, because the field row belongs to that placement; the operator's job is to reach it within tolerance. It removes the robot from the loop while keeping the real stimulator, EMG, tracking and analysis. If a problem disappears in manual mode, it is in the robot or its driver — not in the controller. Caveats Target tolerance matters more. A hand held coil drifts; a pulse whose realised pose is far from the planned one is flagged ( coil was N mm from the planned placement ) and, with a precomputed library, the field used is the planned one, not the delivered one. Check the aim error column in the export. No force feedback. The pressure column is empty and the operator decides the contact. No free drive / objective messages. The Enable free drive button on the Control page has no effect in manual mode. The robot view is empty. There is no simulated robot in robo modes; the Control page shows no 3 D arm. When to use it Commissioning the stimulator, EMG or tracking without the robot. A protocol that requires hand held stimulation. Isolating a fault: if the session runs in manual mode, the controller, relay, InVesalius and stimulator are fine. Training mode is manual positioning with a real stimulator and a virtual EMG. See Run modes and Use cases. Next E field modes The mapping loop

title: Themes and display
blurb: Five colour themes, UI scaling and the display options.
text: Themes and display Five colour themes ship with the controller. They are not skins: every theme defines the same token table, and the style sheet, the charts, the 3 D viewport, the status LEDs, the mode badge and the log bed are all generated from it. Switch a theme Config › Lab › Theme . The change applies immediately — no restart — and is written to /.neuropilot/lab.yaml as UI THEME , so the next session opens with it. You can also pin it from .env : .env wins over the lab profile, like every other key. The five themes Theme Character Good for Workstation Light cool neutral canvas, amber accent the default; screenshots, daylight Lab Paper warm ivory paper, terracotta accent bright rooms, figures for a manuscript Instrument Blue cool slate, deep instrumentation blue keeps amber free to mean "warming up" Graphite dark, neutral two level charcoal long sessions in a dim room Midnight dark, blue black with a cyan accent next to a bright neuronavigation screen The two dark themes are not inverted lights: they define their own status colours and chart series so a red LED is still red, and the accent still passes contrast on the dark canvas.

title: Lab profile reference
blurb: Every ~/.neuropilot/lab.yaml key and the files it controls.
text: Lab profile reference The lab profile is the hardware layer: settings that belong to this machine , shared by every component and by every project. It is a small YAML at /.neuropilot/lab.yaml , edited on Config › Lab . The file Values are stored as strings; the GUI converts them when it reads them. Keys Key Default Meaning RELAY HOST 127.0.0.1 relay address RELAY PORT 5000 relay port ROOT FOLDER /.neuropilot results and plots folder NEUROPILOT UI SCALE empty forced GUI scale UI THEME Workstation Light colour theme ROBOT omron simulated robot key TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH empty tms robot control checkout; used to start the relay automatically INVESALIUS LAUNCH auto auto start policy: auto , local , or off / external (case insensitive) INVESALIUS ENV empty conda environment that contains InVesalius INVESALIUS CHECKOUT empty InVesalius source checkout containing app.py INVESALIUS LAUNCHER empty inv wrapper or other launcher path STIMULATOR PORT /dev/ttyS1 stimulator serial port STIMULATOR TTL PORT /dev/parport0 stimulator TTL port EMG COMPUTER IP 192.168.1.2 EMG acquisition PC address EMG COMPUTER USERNAME neuro SMB user EMG COMPUTER PASSWORD <set in .env SMB password ONLINE FEM SOLVER pardiso FEM solver ONLINE FEM ANISOTROPY scalar conductivity model COLLISION TEST empty saved collision test layout (JSON: head/base poses, start joints, IK branch, safe Z, translation and rotation limits) InVesalius auto start In robo, manual and training mode TMS NeuroPilot starts a local InVesalius before the controller. Simulation does not use InVesalius. With INVESALIUS LAUNCH: auto , this happens only when the relay is local; use local to start a local InVesalius against a remote relay, or off / external to manage it yourself. The INVESALIUS ENV , INVESALIUS CHECKOUT , and INVESALIUS LAUNCHER values are filled automatically after the first successful discovery and can be edited directly in this YAML file. Discovery asks conda for the environment list; CONDA EXE (or a conda executable on PATH ) provides the conda binary. The installer wrapper in the environment is preferred; when it is missing or broken, TMS NeuroPilot uses the environment's Python together with INVESALIUS CHECKOUT/app.py . Closing InVesalius does not stop the controller. The picker also has an Is started option. It sets INVESALIUS LAUNCH: external , skips local startup, and expects an InVesalius instance on another machine to connect to the same relay. When a real/manual/training session starts without a relay, TMS NeuroPilot starts one from TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH . If that path is missing, a directory picker asks for the tms robot control checkout. A value already pinned in .env is updated there; otherwise it is written to this lab profile. Cobot pose and movement limits Config › Lab › Cobot pose shows the same shoulder, arm and wrist choices and the safe Z, translation and rotation limits as the collision test. The values come from the loaded project first, then the COLLISION TEST lab block, then the built in collision defaults. Make project default and Make lab default in the collision test write the complete block. The Config page can also update the lab block with Save lab profile . A loaded project keeps its own values until another project or lab default is applied. Precedence Only keys that the shell and .env leave unset are exported from this file ( os.environ.setdefault ). That is why the GUI marks .env pinned fields and why a value can "not stick": .env is still defining it. Who writes it Config › Lab › Save lab profile writes the hardware keys and merges the Config page cobot pose and movement limits into COLLISION TEST . Config › Lab › Theme writes UI THEME immediately when you change it. The first real/manual/training launch writes the discovered INVESALIUS ENV , INVESALIUS CHECKOUT , and INVESALIUS LAUNCHER values. The controller itself does not write hardware settings; a read only home directory is fine until you press Save. The GUI writes atomically (temp file +

title: Analysis and fits
blurb: How a pulse becomes a regression row and a map of R² over the cortex.
text: Analysis and fits This page explains what happens between "the MEP arrived" and "the map is on screen": the regression matrix, the fit, how R² is computed and the guards around them. From pulses to a matrix For each pulse the controller stores: The analysis ( assemble analysis matrix ) then: 1. drops the pulses the operator excluded, 2. drops the pulses whose E field is None , 3. returns the kept indices and the matching matrix rows. Dropping is never silent: and the MEP history is filtered with the same indices, so row k of the matrix always belongs to MEP k . The three pulse floor The regression needs at least three pulses. Below that the analysis returns without fitting and the GUI keeps saying "No R² map yet — needs at least three pulses." The analysis runs after every third pulse (the ANALYSE step triggers it), and once more at the end of the session. Per channel Each EMG channel is fitted independently: Guards: fewer than three finite MEPs → no map for that channel, [WARN] channel FDI: only 2 finite MEP(s) no map for this channel. some non finite MEPs → those pulses are dropped for that channel only, [WARN] channel FDI: 1 MEP(s) were not measurable and are left out. a length mismatch between matrix and MEP vector → the channel is skipped. The fit functions The nine shapes come from pynibs.expio.fit funs ; the display name is what the project file stores: Display name Shape Linear straight line Linear (log) line against log(response) Sigmoid 4 parameter sigmoid (pynibs' default) Sigmoid (3 parameter) sigmoid with fixed lower asymptote Sigmoid (log) 4 parameter sigmoid against log(response) Exponential exponential with offset Exponential (no offset) exponential through the origin Exponential (log) exponential against log(response) Step step function The "(log)" variants model the logarithm of the MEP; the others the raw peak to peak amplitude. Linear is the default because it needs the fewest pulses to be stable; a sigmoid is closer to the physiological recruitment curve but four parameters need more data. Subsampling map elms (GUI: Subsampling ) analyses every n th ROI element: 1 — every element, the full map; 2 , 3 , … — faster, coarser, fewer multiple comparison opportunities. The value is stored in the project file and refuses to change during a run ( map elms is set when the analysis starts). What R² means here For each element e and channel c : of the fit MEP f(E(e)) across the collected pulses. It measures how much of the MEP variance the field at that element explains. It is not a significance test, and it is not corrected for multiple comparisons across elements; treat it as a localisation aid. Practical reading: Pattern Interpretation one focal hot spot the response is consistent with a source there broad high R² band the field varies smoothly; many elements co vary high R² on few pulses unstable — collect more before interpreting map changes completely after 3 pulses too few samples; wait for 10+ Reporting a map The map is only interpretable together with its acquisition and analysis choices. Record at least: the number of pulses used and the number excluded, with the reason; the fit function and the subsampling factor ( map elms ); the E field mode per pulse, especially for a mixed session; the E field library provenance ( target source , search radius mm , roi hash ) or the online solver settings; the coil model, neuronavigation registration quality and aim error summary; the ROI definition and the element count. Do not report R² as a significance value or as a causal source estimate. A useful figure states the pulse count and the scalar range next to the map. How the analysis runs It runs in a ProcessPoolExecutor , one task per channel, so the GUI and the mapping loop stay responsive. A generation counter invalidates superseded runs: if you exclude a pulse or load another library while a fit is running, the older result is discarded ( discarding a superseded analysis result ). Results are delivered to the GUI

title: Export and data formats
blurb: The results CSV, session records, plots and screenshots.
headings: What is not in the export
text: Export and data formats A session leaves three kinds of files: the results CSV written by the controller, the plots, and whatever you export from the cortical page. This page lists the columns and the formats so an analysis script can be written against them. The results CSV Path: the project's results fn . The final file is written when the session finishes ( Finish ). During the session, the analysis also writes timestamped snapshots next to it ( <name <stamp .csv ), so an interrupted session still leaves the pulses collected so far. Overwrite existing file is on by default, so the final table replaces an existing results fn . If it is off and the path already exists, the existing file is left untouched and the final table is written to <name <stamp .csv instead. Column Unit Meaning idx — position in the target order list (0 based) idx pulse — placement index that was stimulated time — wall clock time of the pulse x realized , y realized , z realized mm coil stimulation point actually used rota realized , rotb realized , rotc realized deg realised coil orientation (XYZ Euler) x target , y target , z target mm planned coil position rota target , rotb target , rotc target deg planned orientation pressure — force sensor reading at stimulation (empty in manual mode) intensity % MSO stimulator output at the pulse e field mode — precomputed , online or surrogate mep <channel mV mV peak to peak MEP per channel mep <channel preact p2p mV pre activation peak to peak mep <channel preact var mV² pre activation variance The MEP columns use the display names from EMG CHANNELS ( mep FDI mV , …). Excluded pulses are not removed from the CSV; the exclusion is an analysis property, so the raw record stays complete. n repetitions = 3 produces three rows with the same idx pulse and different idx . The aim error and the E field are per pulse. Plots Folder Content <ROOT FOLDER /emg plots saved EMG signal plots (Save to .png) <ROOT FOLDER /p2p plots saved MEP trend plots (Save to .png) Folder names come from EMG PLOTS FOLDER PATH and P2P PLOTS FOLDER PATH . The folders are created when their first plot is saved, not when the controller starts. The cortical export Cortical results › Export CSV… writes three files with one base name: <base roi r2.csv Column Unit Meaning element — ROI triangle index, 0 based, same order as the E field columns x mm , y mm , z mm mm triangle centroid, SimNIBS head space r2 <channel — R² per triangle, empty when not fitted <base placements.csv Column Unit Meaning trial — acquisition order pulse index — pulse number in the session target index — planned target index x realized , y realized , z realized mm realised coil centre rota realized , rotb realized , rotc realized deg realised orientation x target , y target , z target mm planned coil centre aim error mm mm distance between realised and planned intensity pctMSO % MSO stimulator output pressure — force reading (empty in manual mode) e field mode — per pulse E field source mep <channel mV mV MEP per channel <base README.txt The column dictionary, generated with the data: Keep this file with the CSVs. It is the only place that states the frame and the units next to the numbers. Screenshots Screenshot… saves the 3 D view as a PNG, including the corner overlays (pulse count, channel, scalar bar). The image is rendered by VTK at the current window size. What is not in the export the E field vectors themselves (they stay in e.hdf5 / the online cache), the raw EMG sweeps (they stay in the plots and the acquisition's own files), the regression parameters per element (only R² is exported), the fit residuals. If an analysis needs the field vectors or the fit parameters, add a dataset to the E field library or extend the export — see Add a component for the code conventions. Reproducing a map To recompute an R² map from an archive you need: 1. the project YAML (which names the files), 2. the E field library ( e.hdf5 ) or the mesh + ROI + coil for an online solve, 3. the resu

title: Add a robot
blurb: One RobotSpec plus two assets makes a new arm usable in the simulator.
text: Add a robot The pipeline is robot agnostic: it sends poses over the relay and reads poses back. Everything robot specific lives in one RobotSpec plus two assets, so adding a robot to the simulator is a table entry. The simulator needs sim robot/robots.py + a MuJoCo model + a URDF. A real robot needs a driver in tms robot control , which is a separate repository with its own configuration. This page covers the simulator; the full recipe, including the real driver side and the relay contract, is in docs/ROBOTS.md . The spec sim robot/config.py derives every robot constant from the spec ( ROBOT URDF PATH , ROBOT BASE BODY NAME , END EFFECTOR SITE NAME , IK ACTIVE LINKS MASK , IK BASE ELEMENTS , IK ELBOW UP , the base pose, the camera framing and MODEL NAME ), so no other file needs editing. The assets Asset Must provide MuJoCo XML the kinematic tree, one hinge joint per actuated axis, actuators named after the joints, a base body, a site at the coil's stimulation point , collision geometry URDF the same chain including the flange and coil holder, so ikpy's tip is the same physical point as the MuJoCo site MuJoCo works in metres and radians; the URDF may use millimetres (ikpy handles its own file). The tool point is the stimulation point , not the flange — a tool point error moves the focus by exactly that error. Validate before starting check verifies that: the files exist and parse, the base body and the end effector site are declared, the URDF contains the base element, the IK mask length equals the chain ikpy builds from the URDF. It exits non zero on a problem and prints a summary of the spec. Select it Config › Lab › Robot — the list comes from the registry; the label is shown and the key is stored. ROBOT=ur5 in .env or /.neuropilot/lab.yaml . ROBOT=ur5 neuropilot sim for one run. An unknown key is reported with the list of known robots instead of silently building the wrong machine. Verify in the simulator 1. neuropilot sim — the view shows the new robot and the head. 2. The arm homes and moves without self collision warnings. 3. A target moves the coil to the head with the handle in the expected direction. 4. The Control log shows Coil at target for a target inside the reach. Real robots tms robot control needs: a driver class that speaks the relay topics ( Neuronavigation to Robot: Set target , … Set objective , … Set free drive , Press robot button , STOP ), a ROBOT CONFIG tuning block, ROBOT=<name in its own .env . TMS NeuroPilot does not change for a real robot: it already sends the same topics the simulator answers. Checklist [ ] check returns 0 [ ] list shows the new key and label [ ] the coil site is the stimulation point [ ] the handle direction matches the physical coil [ ] ROBOT=<key neuropilot sim starts without a traceback [ ] pytest tests/test robot registry.py q passes Next Themes Add a component Relay protocol

title: Add a theme
blurb: The token palette a theme must define and the contrast tests that guard it.
headings: 6. Check the parts a style sheet cannot reach
text: Add a theme A theme is one dictionary of tokens in controller/theme.py . Everything else — the Qt style sheet, the charts, the 3 D viewport, the LEDs, the log bed — is generated from it. 1. Copy an existing theme Pick the theme closest to what you want and copy its block in THEMES : 2. The token contract Every theme must define every token. tests/test theme.py iterates the table and fails on a missing key, so a typo is a test failure, not a black widget. Group Tokens text ink , muted , soft , mono surfaces canvas , card , line , edge , edge hover , hover accent accent , accent dark , accent soft , accent disabled , on accent disabled disabled bg , disabled edge , disabled ink status ok , ok soft , warn , danger , danger soft , danger edge instrument beds bed , bed ink , bed muted , bed sel misc scroll , scroll hover , led off , grid charts series (exactly six colours) 3. Satisfy the contrast tests The tests compute WCAG ratios: Pair Minimum ink on card 7:1 ink on canvas 7:1 muted on card 4.5:1 status colours on card 4.5:1 on accent on accent 4.5:1 ok , warn , danger are also used as text , so they must pass as text, not only as a fill. If your accent is bright, set on accent to a dark ink (that is what Graphite and Midnight do). 4. Pick the mode is dark(name) is computed from the luminance of canvas . It decides which on accent default and which chart treatment is appropriate; it is not a manual flag. 5. Use it Config › Lab › Theme lists the new name automatically (the combo is populated from THEMES ), and UI THEME=My Lab works from .env . The choice is written to the lab profile when changed in the GUI. 6. Check the parts a style sheet cannot reach The theme is applied to more than the window. Open a session and check: [ ] status LEDs (green/red/grey) on Connections, [ ] the mode badge on Config › Lab, [ ] the log bed on Control, [ ] the MEP trend and the EMG trace (series colours and grid), [ ] the 3 D scalar bar and the placement spheres, [ ] the tab strip and its LED corner, [ ] disabled buttons and inputs. 7. Document it Add a row to the theme table in Themes and display — one line on the character and when to use it. A theme nobody can find is a theme nobody uses. Why the tests are strict A theme that "looks fine" on one monitor can make a red LED invisible on another. The contrast tests are the objective floor; they do not replace looking at the actual screen in the lab. Next Themes and display Testing and CI

title: Add a component
blurb: Register relay topics on both sides and plug a new process into the supervisor.
text: Add a component Three kinds of extension share the same rule: the relay is the contract . This page covers a new relay topic, a new process, and the house rules that keep the suite mergeable with upstream. A new relay topic A topic must be handled on both sides, and the simulators must agree with the real components. Place What to add sim robot/config.py a TOPIC constant (if the robot handles it) sim robot/message handlers.py a branch in handle() sim nav/config.py / sim client.py the same for the neuronavigation controller/pipeline controller.py a handler in pub to func (incoming) or a send message call (outgoing) tms robot control the production handler and its topic constant InVesalius (group fork) the PubSub subscription Payload rules: the envelope is {"topic": str, "data": dict} ; the relay routes by event name ( from robot , from neuronavigation , from external controller → to ); everything must be JSON serialisable — convert numpy with .tolist() ; the controller wraps markers in an extra {"data": …} layer because InVesalius' PubSub does; keep that for compatibility; topic names are unprefixed descriptive strings ( Robot to Pipeline: Health status ), matching upstream's style so changes can flow back. The send path drops a message when the client is disconnected and never raises. A misspelled topic looks exactly like a slow system. That is why tests/test relay topics.py asserts the strings on both sides — add your topic to that test. A new component process 1. Create a package under src/neuropilot/<name / with main .py . 2. Register it in supervisor.py : 3. Add it to the sim stack if it belongs there: wait ready is "port" (wait for a TCP port), "line" (wait for the line Connected in its output) or None (no probe). The child runs with its working directory set to the package directory and PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 . 4. Print Connected when the component is registered, so the supervisor and the operator can see readiness. The controller owns a Qt event loop; the robot owns a MuJoCo viewer; the relay owns an aiohttp server. Mixing them in one process produces deadlocks that look like hardware faults. One process per role is the design. House rules for upstream files When the change touches code that also exists upstream ( tms robot control , InVesalius): additive only : a new function or a new branch, with a comment that says why ; removing the addition must restore the original behaviour (± indentation); no group internal BEGIN / END markers and no group prefix in names; do not modify core logic — extend through PubSub where possible; trace the behaviour to the original caller: many near identical functions exist ( CreateMarker / AddMarker / AddMarker ). The full convention is in the workspace AGENTS.md and the project wiki. Testing a new topic and, for behaviour, a unit test that calls the handler with a realistic payload: tests/test relay topics.py is the readable contract; keep it in sync with Relay protocol. Adding a fit function 1. Add the shape to controller/fit functions.py ( FIT FUNCTIONS ), mapping a display name to the pynibs.expio.fit funs callable. 2. Add the name to the tests in tests/test fit functions.py . 3. Add a row to the table in Analysis and fits. The GUI populates its combo from fit names() , so no widget change is needed. Next Relay protocol Testing and CI Add a robot

title: Architecture
blurb: Components, processes, data flow and the repository layout.
text: Architecture TMS NeuroPilot is four processes that talk over one Socket.IO relay. This page is the map: what each process owns, how they start, and where the code lives.

title: Relay protocol
blurb: Topics, payloads and routing between robot, neuronavigation and controller.
headings: Why the topic strings are fixed
text: Relay protocol All components speak one protocol: a Socket.IO event, a topic string and a small JSON payload. This page is the readable contract; tests/test relay topics.py is the executable one. Envelope Units are millimetres and degrees (XYZ Euler, sxyz ) unless a field says otherwise — see Units and frames. Routing Event published by Routed to from external controller to neuronavigation + to robot from neuronavigation to robot + to external controller from robot to neuronavigation + to external controller The relay does not inspect data ; it forwards the envelope. Health and camera frames are broadcast to both peers; everything else follows the table. Topics Controller → neuronavigation Topic Payload Meaning External Controller to Neuronavigation: Create Marker {"data": {"position": [mm], "orientation": [deg], "label": str, "marker type": 3, "is target": true}} create the next coil target Create marker {"label": "stim mark"} mark the stimulation point right after the pulse The extra {"data": …} layer on the first topic mirrors what InVesalius' PubSub expects; Create marker is the short topic used for the per pulse stimulation mark. Neuronavigation → controller Topic Payload Meaning From Neuronavigation: Coil at target markers / pose the coil reached the target From Neuronavigation: Coil target created markers / pose realised target after marker creation Neuronavigation → robot Topic Payload Meaning Neuronavigation to Robot: Set target {"position": [mm], "orientation": [deg]} move the coil here Neuronavigation to Robot: Set objective {"objective": 2} move away from the head Neuronavigation to Robot: Set free drive {"set": bool} enable/disable hand guiding Controller / GUI → robot Topic Payload Meaning Press robot button {"pressed": bool} press the coil against the head STOP {} stop motion now Pipeline to Robot: Set head mesh {"mesh path": str \ null} use this subject head for the simulated phantom; null resets the default Pipeline to Robot: Set start pose {"joints": [rad], "branch": [str]} queue the collision tested six joint start pose and IK branch for the next run Pipeline to Robot: Set motion limits {"safe height mm": float, "translation threshold mm": float, "rotation threshold deg": float} set the direct versus safe height limits for the simulated planner GUI to Robot: set default speed robot {"default speed ratio": float} travel speed GUI to Robot: set tuning speed robot {"tuning speed ratio": float} speed near the head The simulated robot applies Pipeline to Robot: Set start pose and Pipeline to Robot: Set motion limits immediately. The production tms robot control driver does not handle these topics yet; add handlers for the installed robot model before a real run can use project values instead of its .env . Robot → controller Topic Payload Meaning Robot to Pipeline: Health status {"robot id": str, "status": "OK"/"ERROR", "message": str, "info": {…}} the robot card on Connections SIM Robot to Pipeline: Camera frame frame payload simulated camera stream (simulation only) Robot → neuronavigation Topic Payload Meaning Robot to Neuronavigation: Send force sensor data {"force feedback": float} the force gate before a pulse SIM Robot to Neuronavigation: Tracking State {"position", "orientation", "ik success", "collision", "motion done", "tracking valid", "qpos"} simulated tracking (simulation only) Simulation only topics The two SIM topics are the virtual twin speaking: the tracking state lets the simulator drive the neuronavigation without a camera, and the camera frame feeds the controller's robot view. A real robot never sends them. Adding a topic See Add a component. In short: register the constant and the handler in the robot and the nav, handle or send it in the controller, add it to the production components if it must work with hardware, and update tests/test relay topics.py plus this table. Failure semantics The send path is fire and forget : when the client is disconnected, the message is dropped and nothing rai

title: Command line
blurb: Every subcommand and flag, with the environment it expects.
text: Command line Run neuropilot with no arguments to get a small mode selection dialog. neuropilot sim Starts the full simulated stack: relay → neuronavigation ∥ robot → controller. Flag Default Meaning components relay,nav,robot,controller comma separated subset The supervisor waits for each component's readiness probe, prefixes the logs by role and stops everything on Ctrl+C. Exit code 0 on a normal shutdown. neuropilot relay Starts only the simulated relay. Useful when the other components run in separate terminals or on another machine. neuropilot controller Starts only the controller. sim , robo , manual and training are mutually exclusive. For robo , manual , and training , the controller also starts a local InVesalius by default and starts the relay when TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH is configured. Use no invesalius to suppress InVesalius, or invesalius PATH to provide an environment, wrapper, or checkout for this run. neuropilot robo Real hardware mode. Flag Meaning launch relay compatibility flag; a configured relay is started automatically no invesalius do not start InVesalius automatically invesalius PATH use this environment, wrapper, or checkout for this run If no relay is running, the controller starts one when TMS ROBOT CONTROL PATH points to a tms robot control checkout. If the path is not configured, a dialog asks for it and the selection is saved. If the relay cannot be started, the GUI and terminal show the reason and the stack exits. An already running relay is reused. The same relay and InVesalius flags are available on manual and training . neuropilot manual Real hardware, no robot. Same relay behaviour as neuropilot robo . neuropilot training Real stimulator and InVesalius, virtual EMG, no robot. The operator holds the coil and the MEP trace is generated from the E field. Same relay behaviour as neuropilot robo . Start InVesalius before the controller; no robot driver or EMG PC is needed. The channel sources come from the project. Robot registry check validates the MuJoCo model, the URDF, the base body, the tool site and the IK mask. Exit code 1 on a problem. Documentation check is what CI runs; it fails on a broken internal link, an orphan page or a missing nav entry. Tests Data preparation Flags are documented in Subject data and Coil placements. Environment Every command reads the same configuration chain: One off overrides work as expected: Exit codes Code Meaning 0 normal shutdown, or the dialog was closed 1 a required setting is missing (e.g. launch relay without a path), or check found a problem non zero from a child the supervisor stops the stack and exits Cheat sheet Next Run modes Testing and CI

title: Testing and CI
blurb: The test suite, the GUI snapshots and the CI pipeline.
text: Testing and CI The suite has more than 800 tests. Most of them need no display and no hardware; the GUI tests are marked and run on a workstation or in a manual CI job. Running scripts/run tests.sh and .gitlab ci.yml both use scripts/ci python.sh , which finds the interpreter in this order: 1. $PYTHON , if it is executable or on the PATH; 2. the neuropilot conda environment in the usual locations; 3. python3 . Markers Marker Meaning gui builds a real MainWindow ; skipped without DISPLAY / WAYLAND DISPLAY The GUI tests cover all eight pages, resizing, the results table, project load/save with corrupt/empty/missing/binary files, the Config tab against a temporary .env , the study profile, exports and screenshots into deleted folders, manual mode, the status LEDs and recovery buttons, every button on every page, the mesh/coil summary threads and close/teardown. Isolation Tests never touch your data: ROOT FOLDER and the lab/env files are redirected into tmp path ; an autouse fixture fails a test that writes the repository .env , /.neuropilot/last session.yaml or lab.yaml ; GUI tests monkeypatch the session cache path. GUI snapshots tests/test gui snapshots.py captures a 32×24 grey fingerprint and the geometry of every named widget on the seven main pages, and compares them against tests/baselines/gui pages.json . A .ui or style sheet regression fails; the current rendering is left in pytest's tmp path for comparison. After an intentional design change: What the suite proves Area Examples configuration .env round trip with comments, quotes, , backslashes; lab profile precedence; the Config tab's Save split state machine step transitions, skip/back/pause, health holds, step exceptions, monotonic ISI E field per pulse rows, mid run mode switch, solver lifecycle, pulse holds analysis matrix assembly, dropped pulses, per channel NaNs, superseded results data placements validation, library/placement consistency, ROI/mesh loaders GUI pages, buttons, dialogs, exports, screenshots, teardown hardware stimulator/EMG/robot status parsing, relay topics, recovery docs the site builds, every link resolves, every page is in the nav CI pipeline .gitlab ci.yml has two stages: Job Stage What it does check:syntax check compileall on src/ and a pyproject.toml parse — catches a syntax error even without the heavy imports test test pytest m "not gui" with a JUnit report; runs on pushes and merge requests test:gui test manual; pytest m gui on a runner with a display pages (GitHub Actions) deploy builds this site twice from one source: dev → the repository's gh pages branch (<https://tms neuropilot.github.io/tms neuropilot/ , development docs), main → TMS NeuroPilot/tms neuropilot.github.io (<https://tms neuropilot.github.io/ , release docs) The CI variables keep everything isolated: ci python.sh means the runner needs no configuration beyond the neuropilot environment (or a PYTHON variable pointing at it). The documentation build The builder is dependency free (standard library only), so it runs on the same interpreter as the tests and needs no network. It fails on: a page listed in nav.toml that does not exist, a page that exists but is not in nav.toml (an orphan), a broken internal link or asset reference. It also writes search index.json , sitemap.xml , robots.txt and a 404 page. Adding a test Put unit tests next to the existing file for the module. Use the fixtures in tests/conftest.py ( h5file , roi hdf5 , placements hdf5 , e matrix hdf5 , window ), not your own temp files. Mark a test gui as soon as it constructs a widget. Never write outside tmp path ; the guard fixture will fail the test. Coverage gaps Robot motion quality and force control are not tested — they need the physical arm. The real stimulator and the EMG share are mocked; the protocols are tested, the devices are not. The online FEM is tested around the solver, not for numerical accuracy. Screenshot content is fingerprinted, not compared pixel by pixel across machines. Next Architectu
