title: Glossary
blurb: The terms used across the code, the literature and this site.
headings: Internal spellings you may search for
text: Glossary Terms used across the code, the literature and this site. Internal spellings are included so a code search lands here. Stimulation and physiology TMS : transcranial magnetic stimulation. A coil over the scalp induces a brief electric field in the cortex. MSO : maximum stimulator output. Amplitudes in TMS NeuroPilot are % MSO. RMT : resting motor threshold. The intensity at which a MEP appears in about half of the trials; often the reference for the session amplitude. MEP : motor evoked potential. The EMG response to a TMS pulse; its peak to peak amplitude is the quantity the regression uses. Pre activation : EMG activity before the pulse. Displayed and recorded, not used by the regression. ISI : inter stimulus interval. TMS NeuroPilot enforces a minimum ( minium isi , seconds) between pulses. Motor hotspot : the scalp site with the largest MEP for a muscle. Often the target the coil search is centred on. Modelling E field : the electric field a pulse delivers to the cortex, V/m. Recorded per pulse and per ROI element. FEM : finite element method. SimNIBS solves the field on a tetrahedral head mesh. ROI : region of interest: the cortical surface patch the map is computed on. Midlayer : a surface halfway between the grey/white boundary and the pial surface, used as the ROI because it samples the field where pyramidal cells sit. Charm : SimNIBS' head model pipeline (segmentation + meshing). m2m : the SimNIBS output folder m2m <subject with the mesh and the intermediate segmentations. .msh : SimNIBS mesh file, read by TMS NeuroPilot for display and the online solver. .ccd : SimNIBS coil model file (optionally .ccd.nii.gz ). matsimnibs : the 4×4 coil matrix format: rotation in the first three columns, stimulation point in the translation. Stored as (4, 4, n) in placement files, sometimes (n, 4, 4) in E field libraries. E mag : dataset in the E field library, shape (placements, roi elements) . R² : coefficient of determination of the per element fit MEP f(E field) . The map's colour. Fit function : the shape f (linear, sigmoid, exponential, step, and their log variants); nine are available. Subsampling : analysing every n th ROI element ( map elms ). Placement : one coil pose in the search grid. A target is the placement the loop is currently stimulating. Target order : a text file of 0 based placement indices, one per line. Software Relay : the Socket.IO hub that routes {"topic", "data"} envelopes. Topic : the string that names a message, e.g. Robot to Pipeline: Health status . Component : one process: relay, neuronavigation, robot, controller. Supervisor : supervisor.py ; starts components, waits for readiness, multiplexes logs. Simulated twin : the virtual neuronavigation + robot + relay that replace the hardware in neuropilot sim . Online solver : OnlineFEMManager , a SimNIBS/PETSc solve for the realised coil pose during the session. Lab profile : /.neuropilot/lab.yaml ; hardware settings for this machine. Study profile : a YAML with protocol defaults, applied to a session. Project file : the per subject YAML with file paths and session defaults. Session cache : /.neuropilot/last session.yaml ; remembers the last project and settings. NEUROPILOT SESSION FILE moves it for tests and tools. Fit registry : controller/fit functions.py , the mapping from display names to pynibs functions. title: Changelog
blurb: What changed, release by release, and what is still open.
text: Changelog The canonical changelog is CHANGELOG.md in the repository. This page summarises the milestones that change how the suite is used. Unreleased Simulator A new Collision test page runs the selected robot through all project placements in a local MuJoCo scene. It can move the subject head and robot base, jog the coil in world XYZ, choose a shoulder/elbow IK branch, save the start pose to the project and lab profile, and stop at the first collision or IK failure. Four robots now ship with the simulator: Omron TM5X 700, Universal Robots UR5, Han's Robot Elfin E5 (the Aalto / BioMag Helsinki / Tübingen mTMS arm) and Dobot CR5. The tms robot control driver names ( ur , elfin , elfin new api , dobot ) are accepted directly in ROBOT . The head phantom follows the project head mesh in the embedded view: browsing, typing, clearing and project loading all update the simulator; clearing returns to the bundled head.stl phantom. The IK chain is now robot agnostic (active joints are read from the mask, not hard coded slices), and the scene uses the implicitfast integrator. The MSO is snapshotted when each pulse fires. Precomputed, online and interpolated E fields all use that snapshot, so moving the slider afterwards cannot rescale an already recorded pulse. The virtual EMG can use DVS (default, parameters in V/m) or TVS (nine coefficients, normalised to the MSO field). Both read the E field at the configured MEP source element; the Config › Simulation page shows only the selected model's parameters. GUI Large project files (head mesh, ROI surface, coil placements, E field library and EMG source config) are read in background workers. The window stays interactive while they load, each row shows loading... , and Start waits until the reads finish. Changing a path supersedes the older read. Documentation This site: 45 pages covering installation, subject data, every GUI page, every configuration key, the workflows and the reference material. Built by a dependency free generator ( docs/site/build.py ) and published by GitHub Pages on every push to main . Docs are checked in CI: the build fails on a broken link, an orphan page or a missing navigation entry. Robustness The MEP analysis keys ( SAMPLING RATE , CUTOFF FREQ , TMS PULSE TIME , START MEP , END MEP , MEASUREMENT START TIME ) now have defaults in code, so a checkout without .env starts instead of failing at import. The library/placement consistency check now compares matrices stored in either layout ( (4, 4, n) or (n, 4, 4) ) instead of skipping the comparison when the shapes differ. Workflows E field library generation : scripts/02 create roi efield library.py centres the search on the ROI centroid and derives the radius from the ROI extent (+ margin) automatically; n placements 0 keeps the full grid; node based dA/dt makes a solve 4× faster; the output carries provenance attributes (mesh, ROI, coil, target/radius source, grid settings). Interpolated E field mode : the surrogate of Grosshagauer et al. (2025) (code: EfieldInterpolation) is the third E field mode — dense library plus ROI verification ( roi hash ), background load, per pulse interpolation, and a domain guard whose outside policy is skip and exclude (NaN rows). Ships with the auto centred library generator, a validation script and a ParaView time series export. The per pulse regression drops NaN rows (a skipped surrogate pulse) exactly like missing ones. Earlier unreleased work Training mode : neuropilot training runs the real stimulator and InVesalius with a virtual EMG and no robot; the operator holds the coil. Config › Simulation : the five VIRTUAL MEP keys, with the MEP source summary linked to the project. Robot registry — one RobotSpec per robot; list / check ; the Config › Lab selector stores the key and reports unknown values. Five colour themes — Workstation Light, Lab Paper, Instrument Blue, Graphite, Midnight; switchable live from Config › Lab; contrast enforced by tests. Lab profile — hardware settings i

title: About the project
blurb: Who builds TMS NeuroPilot, where it comes from, how it is built and how to cite it.
text: About the project TMS NeuroPilot is research software from the Brain Networks and Neural Data Science and Statistical Computing groups at the Max Planck Institute for Human Cognitive and Brain Sciences ( MPI CBS ) and the Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence ( ScaDS.AI ), Leipzig, Germany. It runs optimized TMS mapping experiments based on per pulse electric fields and integrates with InVesalius neuronavigation to guide TMS placements across many pulses. It performs online mapping analyses, supports robot integration, and ships a complete virtual twin to test and debug workflows without hardware or subjects. It is not a medical device. Real stimulation needs ethics approval, a trained operator and the stimulator's own safety limits. What it is for Run E field optimized mapping experiments with online analysis Simulate mapping results for different optimization functions Switch between precomputed E fields and online E field calculation Put new optimization schemes to the test with a realistic virtual twin Switch mapping parameters live, such as the fit function Exclude single trial responses during a run Train mapping experimenters in realistic settings with simulated MEPs Add new hardware setups, optimization schemes or fit functions thanks to the modular design Scientific scope and limits TMS NeuroPilot implements per pulse E field mapping: each pulse is paired with the field at its realised coil pose, and a regression is fitted separately for each ROI element and EMG channel. This follows the element wise mapping approach described by Numssen et al. (2021) and the TMS mapping protocol of Weise et al. (2023). Coil placement optimisation can use FPS (Schultheiss et al., 2025) or D optimal design (Qiu et al., 2026; Numssen, Qiu et al., 2026). The interpolated E field mode uses the surrogate method of Grosshagauer et al. (2025). The R² map is an explanatory localisation fitted to the collected pulses. It is not a significance map, a causal source reconstruction, or a clinical diagnosis. Report it with the pulse count, excluded pulses, fit function, subsampling factor, E field mode, coil model and registration quality. The cortical results page and analysis page state the guards that limit interpretation. The virtual twin and the virtual EMG are models. They are useful for testing the controller, the relay protocol, the mapping loop and operator training, but they do not replace measurements of a participant's EMG or field. Real stimulation still requires ethics approval and the stimulator's own safety limits.
